brief.thesis: This is an even matchup on the numbers (48.6% Aatrox win rate over 183 games, right in line with Aatrox's 50.2% overall top win rate), and the mechanics explain why: Camille's Q (Precision Protocol, 9/8/7/6/5s) and E (Hookshot, 16/15/14/13/12s) let her pick exact engage windows and disengage before you can punish, while your Q (The Darkin Blade, 14/12/10/8/6s) rewards you for holding position and landing the full three-swing sequence. Whoever controls when the fight happens wins the trade.

theirWindow.when: Her R (Ultimatum) is up at level 6+

yourWindow.when: Her E and Q are both on cooldown
yourWindow.what: She has no engage, no disengage, and no bonus-damage auto up. Step in and land W (Infernal Chains) to pull her toward you, then walk into her for a full Q1-Q2-Q3 sequence since she can't punish or escape the trade.

verdict.line: You win if you poke Sett down with Q swings and E dash-outs and punish his 12-18s Haymaker cooldown, and you lose if you stand in prolonged melee where his Grit shield and missing-health regen erase your damage.

brief.thesis: Sett's Pit Grit passive banks every point of damage he takes into Grit, which his W (Haymaker) spends for a shield plus a true-damage nova, and his passive also grants bonus regen the lower his health drops - so extended slugfests heal and shield him back to even. Aatrox's actual edge is burst-and-reset: land a Q (The Darkin Blade) swing, dash away or reposition with E (Umbral Dash), and only re-engage once his Grit bar and Haymaker are spent. This explains why OP.GG tags Aatrox with lane and solo-kill advantage in isolated trades, yet the measured head-to-head is only 41.9% over 172 games - most Aatrox players are fighting through Sett instead of around him.

yourWindow.what: Without a Grit shield or true-damage burst up, he has no answer to a full Q (The Darkin Blade) combo - commit here, using E (Umbral Dash) to close and its on-hit heal to win the exchange outright.

brief.thesis: Garen's only defensive tool against your engage is Q (Decisive Strike), an 8-second cooldown that breaks slows and silences your next spell — everything else he has is a stationary damage pulse. Camille's E (Hookshot) and Q (Precision Protocol) reset let her pick the exact moment to fight, and the measured 54.3% win rate over 230 games confirms the lane is structurally yours as long as you respect that one cooldown.

theirWindow.when: Q (Decisive Strike) is up and you're in melee
theirWindow.what: He can silence your next ability before all-inning, cancelling your E knockup or Q recast timing — bait it out with an auto or wait it out before committing to Hookshot.

yourWindow.when: your passive shield is active and his Q is down
yourWindow.what: Engage with E (Hookshot) into the knockup, land W (Tactical Sweep)'s outer-cone slow and heal, then walk into the empowered Q recast — he has no tool left to interrupt or disengage.

playing.title: Poke to deny his regen
playing.detail: Land an auto or spell tick on him every few seconds pre-6; his passive only heals if he's untouched for a period, so constant low-grade pressure removes his sustain advantage entirely.

playing.title: Bait his Q before all-in
playing.detail: Decisive Strike breaks slows and silences on an 8-second cooldown. Throw out a spell or poke first to force it out, then commit your full combo once it's down.

playing.title: Use E as the opener, not the finisher
playing.detail: Hookshot needs a wall and knocks him up on landing — use it to start the fight so your W cone slow and Q recast land on a champion who can't walk away.

playing.title: Delay the Q recast in long trades
playing.detail: Precision Protocol's second cast does significantly more damage if you wait between hits — hold it for the tail end of extended skirmishes rather than firing both instantly.

playing.title: Respect his E spin range
playing.detail: Judgment hits nearby enemies at 325 range on a 13-9 second cooldown scaling with level — don't stand in it while trading passively, only enter that range when you're ready to commit.

playing.title: Play proactive, not passive
playing.detail: This is a 54.3% win rate lane over 230 games — freeze the wave against him and look for level 3-5 all-ins rather than sitting back and letting him scale for free.

playing.title: Save R for the finishing blow
playing.detail: The Hextech Ultimatum anchors him in place at 475 range from level 6 — hold it until Trinity Force is online so the fight is already won before you commit it.

brief.thesis: Gwen's Q (Snip Snip!) puts true damage on anything standing in the center of her cone and her passive (A Thousand Cuts) heals her off every auto, so every prolonged melee exchange bleeds in her favor before items. The matchup swings on whether you can land R (The Hextech Ultimatum) on her before she reacts with W (Hallowed Mist), because once that mist is up she can only be targeted by someone who steps inside it.

yourWindow.when: right after Gwen burns W
yourWindow.what: With Hallowed Mist down she's fully targetable, so this is when R actually locks onto her instead of whiffing into an empty mist bubble. Walk her E cooldown first if you can, then commit R plus Q's recast for the delayed bonus damage.

playing.title: Refuse melee trades under level 6
playing.detail: Any prolonged auto exchange lets her Q center hit you for true damage and heals her off the passive. Trade only when her E (Skip 'n Slash) is on cooldown so she can't dash in and refresh attack speed on you.

playing.title: Bait W before you commit R
playing.detail: Hallowed Mist makes her untargetable to anyone outside the mist, so a blind R can whiff. Wait for her to burn it defensively, or walk into the mist yourself before locking on.

playing.title: Use W's outer edge, not the center
playing.detail: Tactical Sweep slows and deals extra damage in the outer half while healing you regardless of where it lands, so aim for poke range rather than point-blank where she can just walk through it.

playing.title: Save Hookshot for a wall, not just distance
playing.detail: E only works off a nearby wall, so track the lane terrain before you need it — both to knock her up into a fight and to bail out of one.

playing.title: Delay your Q recast when you can afford to sit still
playing.detail: Precision Protocol's second cast does significantly more damage if you wait between casts, but it's only 325 range, so this only matters once you're already in her face.

playing.title: Play for the level 9-11 Trinity Force spike
playing.detail: You are behind in raw trading power through most of laning phase; the plan is to survive to that item completion, not to win skirmishes at level 3-5.

playing.title: Track her E cooldown before diving in
playing.detail: Skip 'n Slash refunds its cooldown on hit, so if she's landed it recently assume it's coming back fast — don't commit R into a lane where she still has an escape dash up.

brief.thesis: Illaoi's E (Test of Spirit) forces a binary choice every 16/15/14/13/12s: stand and fight the spirit while it mirrors a percentage of the damage you deal back onto you, or run and become a Vessel that spawns Tentacles for her passive to farm off of. Either answer favors her, which is why OP.GG marks lane and solo-kill advantage in her favor despite the overall matchup being close. Camille has no tool to interrupt E or clear Tentacles from range, so she has to win the matchup on cooldown-reading and scaling rather than raw dueling.

theirWindow.when: She lands W near standing Tentacles
theirWindow.what: Harsh Lesson (W, 4s cooldown) leaps her to you and makes nearby Tentacles swing at you too, healing her off every hit. Back off and let the wave push if you see Tentacles up near a wall.

yourWindow.when: Her W and E are both on cooldown
yourWindow.what: Without Harsh Lesson or Test of Spirit up she has no leap and no mirror-damage threat, so this is when Q (Precision Protocol) auto-trades are actually even. Walk up, take the trade, walk back out before W is back up.

playing.title: Clear tentacles before any commitment
playing.detail: Per OP.GG's own read on this matchup, kill standing Tentacles near walls before you trade or use E (Hookshot) to engage — they will keep swinging and healing her through the entire exchange otherwise.

playing.title: Run from Test of Spirit when losing
playing.detail: If she lands E (Test of Spirit) and you can't win the damage-mirror trade, disengage immediately rather than standing in it — becoming a Vessel means you spawn Tentacles that extend her advantage for the rest of the fight.

playing.title: Trade only when W is down
playing.detail: Harsh Lesson is only a 4-second cooldown at all ranks, so you cannot out-trade her on a timer the way you would against a normal bruiser — wait for the moment right after she uses it before walking up.

playing.title: Save E for repositioning, not opening
playing.detail: Hookshot (E, 16/15/14/13/12s cooldown) needs a nearby wall and only knocks up on landing, so it's a punish tool for catching her out of position, not a safe way to open a trade into her W threat range.

playing.title: Buy into her healing, not around it
playing.detail: Executioner's Calling matters more here than usual — her passive Tentacles heal her on every champion hit, so Grievous Wounds removes a real chunk of her lane sustain, not just a marginal one.

playing.title: Track her ultimate cooldown
playing.detail: Leap of Faith drops from 120s to 70s at rank 3, spawning a Tentacle per champion it hits — don't isolate yourself or a teammate near her once she's level 11+.

playing.title: Survive to your spike, don't force it
playing.detail: This is a defensive lane by design; your job before level 11 is staying even on CS and HP, not finding kills, because the win condition lives in the 11-15 Trinity Force window.

verdict.line: You lose if you trade into her Bladesurge (Q) reset chains and let Ionian Fervor stack to 5; you win if you survive to your Trinity Force spike and only commit R (Hextech Ultimatum) when she's already spent E (Flawless Duet) or R (Vanguard's Edge).

brief.thesis: Irelia's kit is built to punish standing still: Bladesurge (Q) refreshes its full cooldown for free whenever the target is Marked or dies to it, so a low-HP minion near you is a free dash, and Ionian Fervor stacks bonus attack speed off every spell hit until she's adding flat on-hit damage at 5 stacks. Camille has no ranged answer to this — Hookshot (E) only functions near a wall, and Hextech Ultimatum (R) doesn't exist until level 6 and sits on a 140/115/90s cooldown even then. That structural gap is why the measured data has Irelia holding both the lane and solo-kill advantage at a 46.2% Camille win rate over 455 games — play this lane to survive to your spike, not to force it.

theirWindow.when: minions near death, or 5 passive stacks
theirWindow.what: A dying minion next to you is a free Bladesurge (Q) reset that closes the gap without costing her the real cooldown — don't let one sit between you. If she's also at 5 Ionian Fervor stacks, her next few autos carry bonus on-hit damage, so disengage rather than trade through it.

yourWindow.when: when her E (Flawless Duet) is down
yourWindow.what: Without Flawless Duet up she has no stun to punish a commitment, so this is when to step forward with Q (Precision Protocol) and W (Tactical Sweep) for poke. If she opens with E or R (Vanguard's Edge) anyway, answer immediately with R (Hextech Ultimatum) so the anchor and bonus magic damage land before she can follow up.

playing.title: Don't feed her Q resets
playing.detail: Bladesurge (Q) refreshes its entire 10/9/8/7/6s cooldown if the target is Marked or dies to it — protect low-HP minions near you rather than letting her cash one in to dash onto you for free.

playing.title: Track her passive to 5 stacks
playing.detail: Ionian Fervor grants stacking attack speed on every spell hit and flat bonus on-hit damage at max stacks — disengage before a trade lets her reach 5, per the danger threshold in this matchup.

playing.title: Never trade into a charging W
playing.detail: Defiant Dance (W) reduces the physical damage she takes while charging — landing your Q (Precision Protocol) auto mid-charge wastes it, so wait for the release or bait it early.

playing.title: Save R for her E or R
playing.detail: Hextech Ultimatum (R) dashes to and anchors her at 475 range — commit it the moment she opens with Flawless Duet (E) or Vanguard's Edge (R) so her stun or Mark doesn't go unanswered.

playing.title: Only use Hookshot near a wall
playing.detail: Hookshot (E) needs a wall to pull to before it knocks up on landing — plan your engages and resets around lane terrain, since without one it's just a short leap with no knockup.

playing.title: Delay your Q recast for full value
playing.detail: Precision Protocol (Q) can be recast for significantly more bonus damage if you wait between the two attacks — hold the second hit instead of firing it immediately when you need max trade damage.

playing.title: Auto before you expect physical damage
playing.detail: Adaptive Defenses grants a shield versus the damage type of whoever you just basic-attacked — land an auto on her right before an expected physical trade so the shield against her damage is already active.

brief.thesis: Jax's E (Counter Strike) is a single-charge dodge-into-stun that hard-counters short Camille all-ins, which is why he holds both the lane and solo-kill edge across 761 games even though the overall win rate sits at a near-even 48.4%. Camille isn't equipped to win a straight brawl into a live E — she's built to poke with W's cone damage and reset with Hookshot until that charge is burned, at which point her double-cast Q and lockdown kit win the fight outright.

theirWindow.when: his E is up, levels 2-5
theirWindow.what: He will bait a step-in with a half-approach, dodge your first hit, and stun-punish into a full trade. Do not extend Q into melee range here — hold max-range W poke and back off if he walks up.

yourWindow.when: his E is on cooldown or just used
yourWindow.what: Commit immediately: double-cast Q (Precision Protocol) for the true damage proc, then E (Hookshot) to lock the range down. This is the only window where your all-in beats his without item lead.

playing.detail: Once Trinity Force completes, use Hookshot to a wall for long-range engages or split-push and Teleport back to punish overextensions elsewhere on the map.

verdict.line: You lose if Camille lands the level 2 Hookshot all-in before your W is up; you win once Hallowed Mist denies her follow-up and your health-based magic damage scales into her bruiser build.

brief.thesis: Gwen's Hallowed Mist denies Camille the single-target tools she needs to actually kill you — Precision Protocol's empowered auto and the Hextech Ultimatum both require targeting you directly, which fails unless Camille walks into the mist. Meanwhile A Thousand Cuts deals bonus magic damage based on the target's current health, which scales naturally into a max-HP bruiser like Camille. The 50.6% win rate over 816 games and Gwen's measured lane and solo-kill advantage both point the same way: this is a close fight, but the structure favors you.

verdict.line: You lose if he chains Decimate into Crippling Strike and Apprehend before level 6; you win if you survive to Needlework range and he still has to walk through your Hallowed Mist to touch you.

brief.thesis: Darius's entire kill threat is a short-cooldown melee loop — Decimate (Q, 9s down to 5s cooldown) into Crippling Strike (W, flat 5s cooldown) stacking Hemorrhage toward the 5-stack enrage, then Apprehend (E) dragging you back in for a stack-scaled Noxian Guillotine. Gwen has no tool that out-trades him in a standing melee exchange before Needlework comes online at 6, so this matchup is won by denying extended trades and bleed stacks, not by fighting through them.

brief.thesis: Riven's entire kit is burst windows gated by cooldowns you can see expire — Q (Broken Wings, 13s cooldown) and W (Ki Burst, 11/10/9/8/7s cooldown) both have to be up at the same time for her all-in to work. Gwen has no dash to escape a stun, only Hallowed Mist to deny being targeted, so the matchup is decided by whether you poke her cooldowns down with Q (Snip Snip!) before she can line up Q into W.

theirWindow.when: Q and W both off cooldown, level 1-6
theirWindow.what: She can Ki Burst to stun then chain Broken Wings for full combo damage with no way for you to escape since you have no dash. Pop W (Hallowed Mist) the instant she commits so she either backs off or has to walk into the mist to hit you.

yourWindow.when: her Q and W are both down
yourWindow.what: Walk up and land as many Snip Snip! cones as you can — true damage to the center target plus passive stacks — since she has nothing but Valor (E) to block one instance before she has to just eat it.

brief.thesis: Sett's whole kit rewards prolonged melee exchanges — Q (Knuckle Down) empowers his next two autos off max health, his passive heals more the lower his health drops, and W (Haymaker) banks every point of damage he eats as Grit for a shield and true-damage punch. Gwen has none of that sustain; her kit is a hit-and-run cycle of Q poke and E (Skip 'n Slash) dash-ins, not a standing fight. The 46.4% head-to-head over 978 games reflects that Sett wins the fights Gwen's forced into, not the ones she chooses.

playing.title: Play for Counter Strike's cooldown
playing.detail: Jax's E (Counter Strike, 18/16/14/12/10s CD) is his only stun and his only way to dodge autos. When it's down, he has nothing to punish your all-in.

playing.detail: Counter Strike dodges basic attacks, not targeted spell strikes — Q (Bladesurge) still lands even while he's stanced, so it's safe to use to reposition or reset.

playing.title: Never stand and auto-trade
playing.detail: His passive, Relentless Assault, gains attack speed on every strike with bonus damage on every third hit — the longer an auto exchange runs, the worse it gets for you. Win fast with spells.

playing.title: Block the empowered auto with charged W
playing.detail: Jax's W (Empower, 7/6/5/4/3s CD) buffs his next attack. When you see it come up, charge W (Defiant Dance) — it reduces physical damage taken while charging and absorbs the hit.

playing.title: Bank Passive stacks before skirmishes
playing.detail: Keep Ionian Fervor stacked going into any trade so you already have the bonus attack speed and on-hit damage live the moment his E is down.

playing.title: Mark before you dash

playing.title: Respect his early Leap Strike
playing.detail: Jax's Q (Leap Strike, 17/14/11/8/5s CD, range 700) closes distance fast at levels 1-3, matching the data's early solo-kill edge for him — don't overextend for CS in this window.

verdict.line: You lose if you facetank extended trades and let Darkness Rise proc off three landed hits before backing off; you win if you land E's stun-into-Q reset while his W shield is empty and burst him down fast.

brief.thesis: Mordekaiser's W (Indestructible) constantly banks the damage he deals and takes into a shield he can consume to heal, so any trade that doesn't nearly kill him in one window just refuels his sustain. Irelia's answer is to stack Ionian Fervor and chain E's stun-and-Mark into a Q reset for one short, decisive burst rather than grinding an extended fight, then dash out with Q before his passive, Darkness Rise, procs off three landed hits and turns on his damage aura and move speed. That structural coin-flip is why the head-to-head sits almost exactly at 49.9% over 712 games even though Irelia carries the lane-advantage tag — the tools to win are real, but the margin is thin.

verdict.line: You lose this lane if Renekton hits level 2-3 with 50+ Fury and lands a trade, but you win the matchup overall once your armor items come online, matching the 51.5% head-to-head over 1913 games.

brief.thesis: Renekton's power is Fury-gated: at 50+ Fury his W (Ruthless Predator) upgrades from a 0.75s double-slash stun to a 1.5s triple-slash stun that destroys shields, and he has that burst online by levels 2-3 while your Ground Slam is still weak. Once you stack Armor from Sunfire Aegis and Thornmail, E (Ground Slam) scales into real damage and Unstoppable Force gives you the all-in Renekton lacks past mid game, which is why OP.GG measures Renekton with the lane and solo-kill edge but Malphite still holding 51.5% in the head-to-head.

theirWindow.when: Fury above 50%, levels 2-3
theirWindow.what: His W becomes a 1.5s triple-slash stun that strips your Granite Shield and his Q (Cull the Meek) heals harder. Do not stand and trade here; you have no stun of your own until R at level 6, and Ground Slam's attack-speed slow does nothing to stop the stun-lock.

yourWindow.when: Slice and Dice (E) on cooldown
yourWindow.what: That dash starts at a 16s cooldown and only reaches 10s at rank 5, so whenever he's just used it to engage or reset he can't dash away or back in. Shove the wave or stand and trade with Q (Seismic Shard) poke during this window.

verdict.line: You lose if you let Camille auto-trade and walk away between cooldowns; you win the moment you land E and force the fight to go long.

brief.thesis: Camille's whole kit is built around hit-and-run: Q (Precision Protocol) grants bonus Move Speed on an empowered auto, and E (Hookshot) lets her dash to a wall and disengage. Mordekaiser's E (Death's Grasp) pulls all enemies in the area, which erases that disengage the instant it lands, and W (Indestructible) banks the damage from the forced brawl into a shield you can convert to healing. That's why the data shows Mordekaiser holding both the lane win rate (50.8% over 124 games) and the solo-kill edge here — this is a matchup about denying her exit, not out-poking her.

brief.thesis: Sett's passive (Pit Grit) rewards every exchange with alternating left/right punches and missing-health regen, and his Q (Knuckle Down) adds bonus damage on his next two attacks while speeding him toward you — so early trades are built to favor him by design. OP.GG's 52.5% head-to-head over 1,647 games reflects that late reversal, not an easy lane.

brief.thesis: This matchup is decided by one cooldown: Jax's E (Counter Strike), 18/16/14/12/10s. While it's up he can dodge your autos and turn any auto-attack trade into a stun-and-burst for him; the instant it's down he has no answer to your dash-stun-dash combo. The measured 49.6% win rate over 607 games reflects a lane that's genuinely even, decided by who tracks that cooldown better, not by raw stats.

brief.thesis: This is a genuinely even lane (48.9% Sett win rate over 571 games, versus 49.8% for Sett overall) that is decided by trade duration rather than raw stats. Short, decisive trades favor Sett because his Grit resource and Facebreaker (E) stun land before Mordekaiser can profit; long trades favor Mordekaiser because Indestructible (W) turns your damage into his shield and Darkness Rises rewards him for staying in extended contact. Whoever controls how long each exchange lasts controls the lane.

verdict.line: You win if you stun-burst Ornn with E (Facebreaker) and Q (Knuckle Down) before level 6; you lose if the lane drags past his R (Call of the Forge God) and Living Forge's bonus resistances.

brief.thesis: Sett's trading power comes from stacking E (Facebreaker)'s stun with Q (Knuckle Down)'s max-health punches, which is exactly why he holds both the lane and solo-kill advantage here. But Ornn's passive, Living Forge, grants him bonus Armor and Magic Resist from every item he buys, quietly blunting that physical burst the moment he completes his first component, and his R (Call of the Forge God) adds zone-wide Brittle and slows from level 6 onward that let him trade back. That's why the head-to-head sits at 47.3% over 1,614 games — below Sett's 50.6% baseline — the early window is real but closes faster than it does against a non-forging bruiser.

yourWindow.when: Right after Ornn burns Q, E or W
yourWindow.what: Volcanic Rupture (Q), Searing Charge (E) and Bellows Breath (W) are all sub-15s cooldowns early, so the moment he throws one, step in, land Facebreaker (E)'s stun, and dump Knuckle Down (Q)'s empowered punches before he has an escape or knockup ready.

verdict.line: You lose extended trades before level 6 while Renekton's Fury is topped up, but you scale ahead once Stridebreaker and Black Cleaver complete.

brief.thesis: Renekton's Fury bar is the whole matchup: every auto and ability he lands pushes him toward 50 Fury, where Cull the Meek heals harder and Ruthless Predator becomes a three-hit, 1.5s stun that deletes a bad trade. Sett's own resource, Grit, only builds when he is being hit, not when he hits, so Sett cannot out-scale Renekton's Fury spike through auto-trading alone and has to win the lane by baiting cooldowns instead of matching him blow for blow.

brief.thesis: Shen has no sustained damage and relies entirely on E (Shadow Dash) to taunt you into a bad trade, then W (Feint) to no-sell your burst. Sett's whole kit is burst-and-stun, so the matchup is decided by whether you can bait Feint away before you commit Q and E. Data backs this as close to even — 50.5% over 1583 games — with Sett holding the lane- and solo-kill edge, so this is winnable with correct sequencing, not a free lane.

yourWindow.when: Feint (18/16.5/15/13.5/12s) is on cooldown

Without Feint he has zero answer to your burst.

playing.title: Use a minion to land Facebreaker's stun
playing.detail: E (Facebreaker) only stuns if Urgot is pulled in with something on his opposite side — if you're alone with him it just slows. Position so a minion sits behind him before you cast.

playing.title: Play around falling Purge cooldown
playing.detail: Urgot's W (Purge) drops from a 12s cooldown down to 0s at max rank, letting him chain it repeatedly in longer fights. Once he's maxed it, cut trades short instead of standing and out-autoing him.

playing.title: Track his execute threshold
playing.detail: R (Fear Beyond Death) impales and can execute you below a health threshold on a 100/85/70/70/70s cooldown. Don't let your HP sag low mid-trade, and use your own Ignite to deny his escape once you've landed your combo.

playing.title: Hold Show Stopper for the punish, not the opener
playing.detail: R (The Show Stopper, 400 range) is a guaranteed slam and area slow that Urgot's shield can't stop — save it for after Disdain is down rather than opening with it into his shield window.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and every win-rate figure above come from OP.GG's measured Sett-vs-Urgot games on the current patch. The tactical reads on when to trade, bait Disdain, and stack Grit are this brief's own analysis, not measured data.

stats.opponentTip: Avoid being hit by Urgot’s (P) and (E) during early game. Use your lane sustain to fight him using your skills off cooldown to gain lane control.
